correctness.rationale: Two inverse affine branches of Jacobian modulus two give the transfer operator on centered square coordinates. Its exact action on polynomials of degree at most two yields the eigenfunction q-10u/11+2v/11 with eigenvalue 5/8 and exact covariance 8(5/8)^k/45 for all integers k>=0. Finite geometric summation proves the variance formula for every n. The explicit bounded solution h=(5/3)q-(4/3)u+(2/3)v of (I-P)h=Pq gives a reverse martingale difference with checked exact norm 104/135. Saiki et al., Section 3.3, prove the map is Bernoulli; the classical stationary bounded reverse-martingale CLT then proves the stated Gaussian limit. Exact symbolic tests directly verified the quadratic spectral factorization, 25 correlations, 29 finite variances, and branchwise d^2 integral. Infinite conclusions do not rely on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: A natural squared-radius (energy) observable in a vortex-motivated Bernoulli map has a provably slower, sharp 5/8 memory eigenmode than every affine coordinate observable (modulus 1/2). Its full covariance law, all finite-time variances and nondegenerate Gaussian variance quantify a structural contrast between polynomial measurement degrees. The problem is naturally tied to the published model and not an arbitrary parameter slice or renaming; it supplies independently reproducible exact dynamical invariants. It is restricted to degree-two observables in 2D and makes no unsupported global mixing claim.
